task: The city's taxi office gets a raw meter export every month and a separate feed from its official weather station, and trusts neither: some trips run backwards, some fares were reversed, and the station misses hours. Build a pipeline that cleans the trips, measures demand by zone and hour, joins each trip to the weather for its hour, shows from Spark's own plans which way of running the weekly query does the least work, and publishes how rain changes the rides.
problems: Trip times are New York local time; the weather station reports in UTC.
Trips whose dropoff time is before the pickup.
Negative fares and totals from reversed charges.
Pickup and dropoff zone ids 0 and 99, which aren't in the zone list.
The station misses a dozen hours, sends some readings twice, and records missing values as -9999, NaN or impossible numbers.
revenue: A trip counts when it lasted more than 0 seconds, went more than 0 miles and charged a fare above 0. Its revenue is its total: fare, tip, tolls and surcharge. A trip takes the weather of the hour it started in: the station's reading at the next full UTC hour, because a reading describes the hour that ends at it.
